territorial_scope.description: Applies as Arkansas state law, amending the Arkansas Code.

evidence.quote: Arkansas Code Title 18, Chapter 4, Subchapter 1 is amended to add an additional section to read as follows:

summary.short: Adds Ark. Code § 18-4-101 allocating ownership of content generated by, and models trained with, a generative AI tool: to the person giving input or training data, or to the employer where an employee acts within employment under direction. Does not override existing copyright or IP rights.
summary.long: The section, added to Arkansas Code Title 18, Chapter 4, Subchapter 1 (Sec. 1), addresses ownership rather than regulating AI systems. Under subsection (a)(1), when a person uses a generative AI tool to generate content, the person who provides the input or directive owns the generated content, provided it does not infringe existing copyrights or intellectual property rights. Under subsection (a)(2), when a person uses such a tool to conduct model training, the person who provides data or input owns the resulting trained model, provided the training data was lawfully acquired and the person has not transferred ownership rights by contract or agreement. Subsection (b) gives the employer ownership of training data and generated content where an employee is directed to use the tool as part of employment duties, within the scope of employment and under the employer's direction and control. Subsection (c) states that the section grants no ownership over content infringing pre-existing copyrights or other IP rights, regardless of tool use. The text contains no penalty or enforcement provisions and states no effective date.

relations.note: Adds one new section (18-4-101) to this subchapter of the Arkansas Code. Target is a code subchapter, not a registry instrument, so target_instrument_id is left empty.

notes: The document is the bill text, not an enacted or codified version. It contains no effective date, enforcement provision or enactment history, so the registry status 'adopted' is not confirmed by the text. Internal points: subsection (a)(2) calls the person who trains a model the 'owner' of the trained model, while (b)(1) makes training data and generated content 'the property of the individual's employer'. The section heading refers to 'Work made for hire', but the operative text does not use that term. Subsection (a) contains the typo 'aperson', read as 'a person'. Subsection (c) refers generically to pre-existing copyrights and intellectual property rights and names no other instrument.

events.note: The text contains no adoption, signature, publication, entry-into-force, application, deadline or other dated event. Section 1 is the only operative section and states no effective date, and the document has no commencement clause or dated enacting record. Registry metadata (status: adopted) was not used as evidence.

thresholds.note: The text (Ark. Code § 18-4-101, added by HB 1876) sets ownership rules for generative AI model training data, trained models and generated content. It contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its conditions (lawful acquisition, no transfer by contract, scope of employment, direction and control of the employer, no infringement of pre-existing rights) are qualitative.
